newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Foxtel and Australis in merger talks - source.
newsitem.headline: Foxtel and Australis in merger talks - source.

text.p: Pay television groups Foxtel and Australis Media Ltd were holding merger talks but it was not known if an announcement would be made this week, an industry source told Reuters on Monday.

The Australian Financial Review newspaper said that the merger had been agreed to by the key shareholders in each company and was likely to be announced in the next few days once approval had been granted by the anti-monopolies group.
"I don't know whether an announcement is planned this week," the industry sources said.
"No deal has been struck but the fact that these discussions are underway is no secret," the source said.

The newspaper said Australis, which has made losses of nearly A$500 million from an industry that has financially drained all operators, would remain listed on the stock exchange and become majority-owned by Foxtel partners News Corp Ltd and Telstra Corp under the deal.

It also said Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd, a major shareholder in Australis and its largest local financier, would become a partner with News Corp in the rationalisation of the industry.
A merged Foxtel/Australis would directly challenge the only other key player in pay television, Optus Vision, which has more than 180,000 subscribers.
Foxtel has about 200,000 subscribers while Australis has a little more than 100,000 with its satellite-based service.
Australis shares rose one cent to end at 15 cents on Monday in a weaker overall market.
